milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because the evaluator's voxel system cannot detect door block state changes (open=true vs open=false) — the block type remains 'oak_door' regardless of state. This rule verifies the player navigated within very close interaction range (1.5 blocks) of the oak door at spawn-relative (0, 0, 6) and is facing it (within ±30° of the door direction). The tight 1.5-block distance ensures the player is close enough to have interacted with the door via right-click, making this the strongest available proxy for door-opening verification.

The player spawns on a flat stone brick floor with a clear, unobstructed path to the door approximately 6 blocks ahead. The structure is a simple enclosed room (7x5x4) with the door centered in the front wall. The surrounding area is cleared of vegetation to ensure unobstructed navigation.
task_text: Walk to the stone brick building ahead and open the oak door.
design_notes: Player spawns facing north (+Z direction). Stone brick floor extends from ~-5 to ~5 in X and ~-5 to ~15 in Z. All blocks above the floor are cleared to prevent tree/vegetation interference. The room's front wall is at Z+6 with the door centered at (X=0, Y=0, Z=6). Door faces south so it opens correctly when approached from the south. Interior cleared (Z=7 to Z=9) for door swing space. The 6-block distance from spawn to door is easily traversable within 20 steps.
